analysis.investment_thesis: Clean Science is a genuinely excellent specialty chemicals business — zero debt, 27.3% ROCE sustained over multiple years, and a dominant position in performance chemicals like MEHQ and TBHQ. However, at an earnings yield of only 4.8% (EBIT INR 388 Cr / EV ~INR 8,034 Cr), the Magic Formula says the price already reflects the quality and there is no 'cheap' cushion.
key_strengths: ROCE of 27.3% and operating margins of 24% reflect genuine competitive advantage in green chemistry processes with low waste and high capital efficiency
Virtually debt-free balance sheet (borrowings INR 2 Cr) with 7-year revenue CAGR of 22% and profit CAGR of 27%, showing durable compounding
Diversified export markets (Americas, Europe, China) and multi-segment exposure (Performance, FMCG, Pharma/Agro) reduces concentration risk
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~4.8% is well below the 6% Magic Formula floor — you are paying a full price for a known good business with limited margin of safety
FY2024 showed a profit dip (INR 295 Cr → 244 Cr) before partial recovery; capex has been heavy (INR 232 Cr in FY2024) with CWIP rising to INR 98 Cr, pressuring near-term FCF
Specialty chemicals is subject to pricing pressure from Chinese overcapacity and customer inventory destocking, as evidenced by FY2024 revenue decline
red_flags: FCF was negative in FY2022 (-12 Cr) and near-zero in FY2024 (10 Cr) due to heavy capex cycles — FCF conversion is inconsistent
Revenue dipped from INR 936 Cr (FY2023) to INR 791 Cr (FY2024) before recovering — suggests demand volatility, not a pure compounder
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On Magic Formula mechanics: EBIT/EV = INR 388 Cr / ~INR 8,034 Cr = 4.83% earnings yield — below my 6% threshold. ROCE of 27.3% is genuinely excellent and sustained across multiple years, confirming this is a high-quality business. But the formula demands BOTH cheap AND good; here we only have 'good.' The business earns above its cost of capital by a wide margin, but the market has already priced that in at 32.8x P/E and 20.4x EV/EBITDA.

The expansion capex (CWIP growing to INR 98 Cr) suggests management is investing for the next leg of growth, which is sensible for a high-ROIC business. However, FCF has been lumpy — only INR 72 Cr in FY2025 on INR 264 Cr of net profit implies capital consumption. I would watch for ROIC dilution if the new capacity comes online at lower utilisation rates. A Magic Formula investor should put this on a watchlist and buy on any meaningful price correction toward 12%+ earnings yield.
